  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 1
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation
Date:  March 6, 2023
Subject:  Proposed Program Fees for 2023/24

Recommended Motion:  Approve the Proposed Program Fee Schedule for May 12,
2023, to May 11, 2024.

Report Summary: On a regular basis, the Parks & Recreation Department reviews the
fees they charge for different programs offered by the Department so that they can be
brought in-line with the costs to provide the programs. Annually, we bring to the
Commission a report on the fees and any proposed changes that are being
recommended for the upcoming fiscal year.

In FY 2021 & 2022, the minimum wage increase went from $13.00 per hour to $14.00
per hour, and finally to $15.00 per hour. No increases to class fees were implemented
at these times due to Covid issues cancelling the majority of Parks & Recreation
Department classes. Starting in FY2023 staff recommended an increase of 10% per
program to catch up to minimum wage increases and inflation.

As the Commission is aware, inflation has not slowed down (5.81% higher than last
year), and the Minimum Wage in California was increased from $15.00 hr. to $15.50 hr.
in January of this year. Thus, staff is recommending an overall 7% increase in program
fees for next fiscal year to keep up with ever rising costs. This pricing will be applied to
the Summer registration period that will start in May of this year.

The only exceptions to the price increase will be our Tot Time program which has seen
a significant drop in registrations due in large part to LAUSD adding PreK programming
to many of their campuses for free. Thus, the registration of families with 4- to 5-year-
olds has been reduced and the majority of the children are just 3 years old. For this
reason, we are recommending keeping the program at the same pricing from FY22/23.

In addition, staff believes that the membership program for the Sports Center Fitness is
currently competitive with other businesses that are offering the same product and any
increase will negatively affect the numbers of registrations. With this in mind, the
recommendation is to keep the pricing the same, but to increase marketing so that

  5
 some of the revenue can be made up through volume of registrations and not just an
overall price increase.

Report Summary: Each year the commission reviews the Department’s current
concession agreements and provides staff with recommendations, particularly for those
agreements that are currently up for extension or renewal. Concession agreements are
typically those that allow a private business, either for profit or non-profit, to conduct
business on Park property or to operate a program on behalf of the City.
On the following page is a list of the concession agreements that are currently active
along with information regarding their expiration dates.

Staff is pleased with all current operations and is recommending that all possible
extensions be implemented.
